findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4146 is the Webtools Add-on (TA-webtools). The Splunk Add-on for Salesforce is 3549, which sibling UC-23.3.2 uses. The same wrong ID is repeated in references.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to Splunk Add-on for Salesforce (Splunk_TA_salesforce, Splunkbase 3549) in app and references.

findings.explanation: Google Ads API has no `metrics.quality_score`. Quality Score is a keyword-level attribute, `ad_group_criterion.quality_info.quality_score`, queried from `keyword_view`. Campaign-level GAQL rows as described will therefore never carry a Quality Score, and the QS band logic is always 'unknown'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a keyword_view GAQL pull selecting `ad_group_criterion.quality_info.quality_score` (plus creative/post-click/predicted-CTR buckets), and say that QS is rolled up to the campaign level, for example impression-weighted.

findings.explanation: Google Ads API v17 was sunset long ago; the current reference is v24/v26. Pinning a sunset version makes the polling instructions fail. The same pin appears in app, evidence and detailedImplementation, where 'API v17 deprecation' is presented as a troubleshooting item.
findings.quote: Google Ads API v17 — GAQL polling
findings.suggested_fix: Do not pin a version, or say 'a currently supported Google Ads API version (see the sunset schedule)'.

findings.explanation: Oracle ended Moat Analytics on 30 September 2024, so the MOAT feed, the `moat:sivt` sourcetype and the `moat_score` filter cannot be implemented. The evidence field also cross-references MOAT reports.
findings.quote: Configure HEC for SIVT-overlay reports from MOAT (`/v2.4/inventory`) and DoubleVerify ... `where moat_score>=70 AND doubleverify_score>=70`
findings.suggested_fix: Replace MOAT with a current verification vendor (DoubleVerify, IAS) or drop the SIVT overlay. Remove MOAT from evidence.

findings.explanation: The implementation steps build a different detection from the canonical SPL. It uses a different index (vs `index=business`), different sourcetypes (vs `paid_media:*`), a 15-minute/2-hour window (vs 30-day CPA rollups with week-over-week deltas), and a different z-score SPL with SIVT filters. A reader following these steps produces data the canonical search never matches.
findings.quote: Forward to Heavy Forwarders sending to `index=marketing_paid_media` with `sourcetype=google_ads:campaign_metrics`, `sourcetype=meta:insights` ... `cron_schedule = */15 * * * *`, `dispatch.earliest_time = -2h` ... Use SPL: `index=marketing_paid_media ...`
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the steps to ingest into `index=business` with the `paid_media:*` sourcetypes from dataSources, schedule the canonical SPL (e.g. daily), and delete the alternative inline SPL.

findings.explanation: This appears in detailedImplementation step 2. props.conf says not to combine INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS=json with KV_MODE=json, because fields are extracted twice. TIMESTAMP_FIELDS lists the fields that together form one timestamp, not one alternative per vendor.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one props stanza per vendor sourcetype with its own timestamp field. Pair INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS=json with KV_MODE=none, or use KV_MODE=json alone for HEC event payloads.

findings.explanation: UC-23.3.6 is Content Marketing & Resource-Center Lead Conversion and UC-23.3.7 is Email Deliverability; neither covers influencer, affiliate or CTV. DV360 is also listed as an in-scope source in dataSources (`dbx:dsp_spend`), which contradicts the exclusion.
findings.quote: Influencer / creator-marketing performance excluded (covered by UC-23.3.6). Affiliate-network performance (CJ Affiliate, Impact, Awin) tracked in UC-23.3.7. ... Programmatic CTV / DV360 ... handled in UC-23.3.6.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the wrong UC references and settle whether DSP/DV360 spend is in scope.

findings.explanation: These are unit-normalisation branches, not alert conditions. The SPL flags campaigns whose blended CPA exceeds the platform target, whose CPA rose more than 25% week over week, whose LTV-adjusted ROAS is below the floor, or that spent more than $5,000 with Below-Avg Quality Score.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the four alert conditions and the per-campaign, per-platform 30-day grain.

findings.explanation: These scenarios are generic. The real paid-media false-positive causes are missing: Smart Bidding learning periods after strategy changes, conversion-reporting lag and attribution-window back-fill, FX rate gaps, budget changes mid-month, platform-reported versus CRM-deduplicated conversions, and iOS ATT under-reporting. detailedImplementation hints at some of these.
findings.quote: Synthetic probe on `quality_score_band`, `platform`, `account_id`, `campaign_id` — Health checks in `business` populate the same fields
findings.suggested_fix: List the paid-media causes with mitigations (exclude campaigns in learning status, lag the window by the attribution window, require FX rows).

findings.explanation: Dell EMC storage has nothing to do with paid-media CPA analytics.

Reloading the deployment server does not refresh OAuth credentials on a Heavy Forwarder. tstats must be the first command in a search. `/v2/adAnalyticsV2` is the legacy LinkedIn endpoint, while dataSources uses `/rest/adAnalytics`. TikTok `/business/get/` is not the ads reporting endpoint (`/report/integrated/get/`).
findings.quote: reload with `splunk reload deployment-server` ... `| search index=marketing_paid_media | tstats latest(_time) where index=marketing_paid_media` ... LinkedIn Ads (`/v2/adAnalyticsV2`), TikTok OAuth (`/business/get/`)
findings.suggested_fix: Say to update the credential in the add-on's storage/passwords and restart the input. Use `| tstats latest(_time) where index=business sourcetype=paid_media:*`. Use the same LinkedIn and TikTok endpoints as dataSources.

findings.explanation: The reviewer is an authoring agent. A discontinued vendor, a sunset API version and the wrong add-on ID show the content was not verified.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the status to draft/community until a marketing-ops or Splunk SME validates it.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Dotted field names are unquoted inside coalesce (`metrics.cost_micros`, `metrics.impressions`, `metrics.quality_score`, `ad_group.id`). In eval, `.` is the concatenation operator, so these do not reference the GAQL fields. Single-quote them as done for `'campaign.id'`.

`bin _time span=7d` and the week-over-week `streamstats` run after a `stats` that dropped `_time`, so there is one row per campaign and `cpa_delta_pct` is always null. Join keys also mismatch: numeric `campaign_id` is joined against lowercased UTM slugs and CRM CampaignId.
`fillnull value=999999 target_cpa_threshold` and the default `monthly_budget_usd=250000` hide missing lookups. `pacing_health` treats the 30-day spend total as month-to-date.

summary: The UC has a broad, plausible multi-platform paid-media data inventory. But several product facts are wrong: the Salesforce add-on ID, the Quality Score field, the Google Ads API version, MOAT (discontinued) and the props settings. detailedImplementation describes a different index, different sourcetypes, a different schedule and a different SPL from the canonical search. Exclusion cross-references and templated fields misdescribe the detection.
